newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Radical Chechen rebel commander said badly hurt.
newsitem.headline: Radical Chechen rebel commander said badly hurt.

text.p: An aide to radical Chechen rebel commander Salman Raduyev said on Friday that his boss, one of Russia's most wanted men, had been critically injured in an assassination attempt.
Sultan Miyev, Raduyev's military consultant, told Reuters in the Chechen capital Grozny that Raduyev's car had been blown up early on Wednesday on a road outside the city.
"He is very seriously injured. He underwent an operation but it was not successful. He is in critical condition in hospital," Miyev said.
Chechen officials were not immediately available for comment, but Russian news agencies quoted them as saying they had no reliable information about the incident.
RIA news agency quoted Chechnya's Interior Ministry as saying it had no details of the assassination attempt. But the agency said ministry officials refused to deny the reports.

RIA added that doctors in Grozny hospital, where Raduyev was reported to have been taken after Wednesday's incident near the town of Urus-Martan some 20 km (12 miles) away, could not confirm that he was there.
Raduyev, wanted by Russian police for masterminding a bloody armed raid in the Russian region of Dagestan bordering Chechnya last January, was reported killed in an ambush last year.
He later resurfaced, saying he had been seriously hurt but had undergone plastic surgery in Germany. His face was barely recognisable.

Miyev blamed Russia for staging the assassination attempts and promised revenge attacks The Chechens frequently blame Russian agents provocateurs for trouble in their Caucasus region, charges which Moscow rejects.
The Russian Interior Ministry denied any connection to the reported attack on Raduyev.

Miyev promised one attack on Russia to avenge Raduyev and one to avenge former Chechen President Dzhokhar Dudayev, believed killed in a Russian rocket attack last April 20 during the 20-month conflict over Chechnya's independence drive.
"I want to say as military consultant to Raduyev's army that on April 21 or 22 there will be a revenge blow in Russia. The Russians will find out for themselves when and in what towns," he said.

Itar-tass news agency quoted the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) as saying that threats to launch attacks on Russian territory were part of provocations aimed at undermining peace process in the North Caucasus region.
"We closely investigate all statements about planned terrorist acts no matter what the source," FSB spokesman Alexander Zdanovich said.
Raduyev has vowed several times to launch attacks in Russia but none has materialised.
It is not clear how many armed supporters he has, although Chechnya, where rebels fought a 21-month war with Russian troops sent to crush an independence bid, is still awash with weapons.

Russia and Chechnya stopped fighting under a ceasefire signed last August and Russia pulled all its forces out, but peace talks are bogged down over Chechnya's political status. Chechnya wants full independence but Russia rules this out.
